scope: New Go domain types only, in internal/pipeline: RunStatus, Mode, Run struct (ID, SessionID, Mode, Status, CurrentStage, StartedAt, FinishedAt), and pure Start/Advance/Fail/Cancel invariant methods, plus a new kernel.RunID strong ID type. No orchestrator, no service.go, no store/persistence, no Gin/HTTP, no LLM, no time.Now() calls (caller supplies 'now', matching shared/clock's Clock.Now() contract). Table-driven tests only, pure behavior.

acceptance_criteria.text: RunStatus constants match run_status enum exactly: pending, running, done, failed, cancelled. Mode constants match session_mode exactly: planning, descriptive, visualize.

Run struct fields map 1:1 to pipeline_runs columns relevant to in-memory state (id, session_id, mode, status, started_at, finished_at) plus CurrentStage as the in-process stage cursor (not a DB column — pipeline_stages rows track per-stage persistence, out of scope).

Start(now): pending->running only, sets CurrentStage=pipeline.Order[0], StartedAt=now. Advance(now): running only, moves CurrentStage to pipeline.Order[i+1]; when CurrentStage is already the last stage, transitions Status->done and sets FinishedAt instead (confirmed with user: no separate Finish/Complete method). Fail(now)/Cancel(now): any non-terminal status -> failed/cancelled, sets FinishedAt; no reason argument (confirmed with user: pipeline_runs has no error column, so Fail/Cancel stay bare). All four return a single sentinel ErrInvalidTransition on misuse; none call time.Now() internally.

run_test.go table-driven, covering: Start from pending (ok) and from every other status (error); Advance through all 6 forward steps plus auto-done from result; Advance while not running (error); Fail/Cancel from pending and running (ok) and from each terminal status (error). go test passes.

risks: CurrentStage's zero value (empty string) represents 'not yet started' — before Start() is called, Run.CurrentStage is not a valid pipeline.Stage. Documented via a zero-value comment on the field rather than a separate wrapper type, to avoid introducing an Optional[Stage] abstraction nothing else needs yet.
